symbols.name: D
symbols.def: Number of observed variables.

symbols.name: K
symbols.def: Number of non-observational regimes.

symbols.name: S
symbols.def: A finite set of selection vertices disjoint from \(V\).

symbols.name: X
symbols.def: \(X=(X_v)_{v\in V}\) is the observed reality-world random vector, with every \(\mathcal X_v\) finite.

symbols.name: S_star
symbols.def: \(S^*=(S_s^*)_{s\in S}\) is the counterfactual basal-world selection-status vector; a unit is observed exactly on \(S^*=\mathbf 1\).

symbols.name: zeta
symbols.def: \(\zeta=(\zeta_1,\ldots,\zeta_K)\) are distinct regime-indicator vertices disjoint from \(V\cup S\); \(\zeta_k\) is included only in regime \(k\)'s MAG.

symbols.name: U_k
symbols.def: \(U_k\) is the full observed-plus-indicator vertex domain of regime \(k\)'s MAG; \(U_0\) has no intervention indicator.

symbols.name: G_DK
symbols.def: \(\mathcal G_{D,K}\) is the ambient space of graph, selection, target, and local-kernel tuples indexed by \(D\) observed vertices and \(K\) intervention regimes.

symbols.name: T
symbols.def: For each selected-intervention model \(g\in\mathcal G_{D,K}\), \(T(g)=(T_1(g),\ldots,T_K(g))\) is its latent family of direct soft-intervention targets.

symbols.name: G0
symbols.def: For a model tuple \(g\in\mathcal G_{D,K}\), \(G_0(g)\) is its basal selected DAG on the disjoint vertex union \(V\cup S\).

symbols.name: kappa
symbols.def: For \(g\in\mathcal G_{D,K}\), \(\kappa_v^{(j)}(g)(dx_v\mid x_{\operatorname{pa}_{G_0(g)}(v)})\) is the regime \(j\) local conditional kernel at vertex \(v\).

symbols.name: eta
symbols.def: \(\eta=(S,G_0(\eta),(T_k(\eta))_{k=1}^{K},(\kappa^{(j)}(\eta))_{j=0}^{K})\) is a fully specified selected-intervention model tuple.

symbols.name: P_sel
symbols.sig: \(P_{\eta}^{(0)}=\mathcal L_{\eta}(X\mid S^*=\mathbf 1),\qquad P_{\eta}^{(k)}=\mathcal L_{\eta}(X\mid S^*=\mathbf 1,\text{ regime }k),\quad k\in[K]\)
symbols.def: The observational selected law is defined separately by \(P_{\eta}^{(0)}:=\mathcal L_{\eta}(X\mid S^*=\mathbf 1)\); this is the only selected law when \(K=0\) and it contains no intervention index or indicator. For \(K\ge 1\) and each \(k\in[K]\), \(P_{\eta}^{(k)}:=\mathcal L_{\eta}(X\mid S^*=\mathbf 1,\text{ regime }k)\) is the selected intervention-arm law.

symbols.name: P_pool
symbols.def: For \(K\ge 1\) and \(k\in[K]\), \(P_{\eta,k}^{\mathrm{pool}}\) is the equal-weight binary-indicator law on \(X\cup\{\zeta_k\}\) that assigns \(P_{\eta}^{(0)}\) to \(\zeta_k=0\) and \(P_{\eta}^{(k)}\) to \(\zeta_k=1\). No pooled law is defined when \(K=0\).

symbols.name: M_DK
symbols.def: \(\mathfrak M_{D,K}^{\mathrm{Dai}}\), defined in \(\mathrm{def:model-class}\).

symbols.name: M_k
symbols.type: ordered maximal ancestral graph family map
symbols.def: \(M_0(\eta)\) is the observational latent projection on \(U_0=V\) associated with \(P_{\eta}^{(0)}=\mathcal L_{\eta}(X\mid S^*=\mathbf 1)\). For \(k\in[K]\), \(M_k(\eta)\) is the latent projection on \(U_k=V\cup\{\zeta_k\}\) of the interventional twin graph whose observed law is the pooled selected law \(P_{\eta,k}^{\mathrm{pool}}\).

symbols.name: O
symbols.def: \(\mathcal O(\eta)=\bigl(\operatorname{skel}(M_k(\eta)),\operatorname{UC}(M_k(\eta))\bigr)_{k=0}^{K}\), where both components are taken on the full regime domain \(U_k\). Its \(k=0\) component is the observational signature associated with \(P_{\eta}^{(0)}=\mathcal L_{\eta}(X\mid S^*=\mathbf 1)\), with no indicator. For every \(k\in[K]\), \(M_k(\eta)\) is interpreted through the pooled selected law \(P_{\eta,k}^{\mathrm{pool}}\), not through either arm law alone, and the signature retains every adjacency and every unshielded collider involving only vertices in \(V\) or involving \(\zeta_k\).

symbols.name: C_O
symbols.def: \(\mathcal C(\mathcal O)=\{\eta\in\mathfrak M_{D,K}^{\mathrm{Dai}}:\mathcal O(\eta)=\mathcal O\}\).

symbols.name: E_O
symbols.def: \(\mathcal E(\mathcal O)\) contains the endpoint positions on observed--observed adjacencies of the full MAGs \(M_k(\eta)\), \(k=0,\ldots,K\). Endpoints at \(\zeta_k\) are retained in \(\mathcal O\) as constraints on the fiber but are excluded from this reported endpoint domain.

symbols.name: mu
symbols.def: \(\mu_\eta(e)\) is the endpoint mark at the observed endpoint position \(e\) in the corresponding induced graph \(M_k(\eta)[V]\).

symbols.name: P_SI
symbols.def: \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{SI}}(\mathcal O)\) records, on \(\mathcal E(\mathcal O)\), the observed-endpoint mark common to all \(\eta\in\mathcal C(\mathcal O)\), and a circle otherwise. The compatibility fiber uses the observational \(U_0=V\) signature associated with \(P_{\eta}^{(0)}\), and, for every \(k\in[K]\), the complete \(U_k\)-level adjacency and unshielded-collider signature of \(P_{\eta,k}^{\mathrm{pool}}\), including all \(\zeta_k\)-involving constraints.

symbols.name: O_0
symbols.def: \(\mathcal O_0(\eta)=\mathcal I(M_0(\eta))\) is the full set of conditional-independence relations encoded by the observational MAG on \(V\); it therefore fixes the complete observational Markov-equivalence class used by Zhang's PAG.

symbols.name: E_0
symbols.def: \(\mathcal E_0(\mathcal O_0)\) contains the two endpoint positions of every adjacency common to the observational Markov-equivalence class indexed by \(\mathcal O_0\).

symbols.name: C_MAG0
symbols.def: \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{MAG}}(\mathcal O_0)=\{M\in\operatorname{MAG}(V):\mathcal I(M)=\mathcal O_0\}\).

symbols.name: C_Dai0
symbols.def: \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{Dai}}(\mathcal O_0)=\{M_0(\eta):\eta\in\mathfrak M_{D,0}^{\mathrm{Dai}},\ \mathcal O_0(\eta)=\mathcal O_0\}\).

symbols.name: nu
symbols.def: \(\nu_M(e)\) is the endpoint mark at \(e\) in an observational MAG \(M\in\mathcal C_{\mathrm{MAG}}(\mathcal O_0)\).

symbols.name: P_Zhang
symbols.def: \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{Z}}(\mathcal O_0)\) records an endpoint mark when \(\nu_M\) has that mark for every \(M\in\mathcal C_{\mathrm{MAG}}(\mathcal O_0)\), and records a circle otherwise.

symbols.name: A
symbols.def: For each model \(\eta\), \(A(\eta)=\operatorname{An}_{G_0(\eta)}(\operatorname{pa}_{G_0(\eta)}(S))\cap V\), including the observed selection parents.

symbols.name: C_fixA
symbols.def: \(\mathcal C_A(\mathcal O,\eta)=\{\widetilde\eta\in\mathcal C(\mathcal O):A(\widetilde\eta)=A(\eta)\}\).

symbols.name: F
symbols.def: \(F_k(\eta)\) is the set of observed variables directly or indirectly affected by regime \(k\)'s direct target set \(T_k(\eta)\).

symbols.name: H
symbols.def: The observational skeleton in \(\mathcal O\).

symbols.name: Z
symbols.def: \(Z=(Z_1,\ldots,Z_K)\), where \(Z_k=\operatorname{adj}_{M_k(\eta)}(\zeta_k)\cap V\), is read from the full signature \(\mathcal O\). By Dai et al.'s Lemma 5, \(Z_k=T_k(\eta)\cup((F_k(\eta)\setminus T_k(\eta))\cap A(\eta))\); hence \(Z_k\) contains direct targets together with any indirectly affected ancestrally selected variables and need not equal \(T_k(\eta)\).

symbols.name: sigma
symbols.def: \(\sigma(v)=\{k\in[K]:v\in Z_k\}\).

symbols.name: L_A
symbols.def: \(x\to y\in L_{A(\eta)}\) iff \(xy\in H[A(\eta)]\) and \(\sigma(x)\subseteq\sigma(y)\).

symbols.name: Reach_A
symbols.def: \(\operatorname{Reach}_{A(\eta)}(x,y)=1\) iff \(L_{A(\eta)}\) contains a nonempty directed path from \(x\) to \(y\).

symbols.name: C_sel
symbols.def: \(\mathsf C_{\mathrm{sel}}(\mathcal O)\) is the least observable vertex set defined in \(\mathrm{def:observable\mbox{-}selectedness\mbox{-}closure}\).
symbols.role: observable surrogate for certified selection membership

symbols.name: L_cert
symbols.def: \(x\to y\in L_{\mathrm{cert}}(\mathcal O)\) if and only if \(xy\in H[\mathsf C_{\mathrm{sel}}(\mathcal O)]\) and \(\sigma(x)\subseteq\sigma(y)\).

symbols.name: Reach_cert
symbols.def: \(\operatorname{Reach}_{\mathrm{cert},\mathcal O}(x,y)=1\) if and only if \(L_{\mathrm{cert}}(\mathcal O)\) contains a nonempty directed path from \(x\) to \(y\).

symbols.name: B
symbols.def: An acyclic signature-monotone subgraph of \(H[A(\eta)]\) with no new unshielded collider.

symbols.name: RepGraph
symbols.def: \(\operatorname{RepGraph}(\eta,B)\) is the purely graphical replacement specification constructed in \(\mathrm{def:basal\mbox{-}replacement}\); it contains a basal selected DAG and direct-target sets but no probability kernels.

symbols.name: Real
symbols.def: \(\operatorname{Real}(\eta,B)=\{\widetilde\eta\in\mathfrak M_{D,K}^{\mathrm{Dai}}:(G_0(\widetilde\eta),(T_k(\widetilde\eta))_{k=1}^{K})=\operatorname{RepGraph}(\eta,B)\}\). Membership fixes only the replacement graph and direct-target data; every member carries its own fully specified kernel family.

symbols.name: G_san
symbols.def: \(\mathsf G_{\mathrm{san}}\) is the explicit \(D=3\), \(K=1\) graph-and-target specification in \(\mathrm{def:retained\mbox{-}edge\mbox{-}sanity\mbox{-}specification}\).

symbols.name: Lambda_SI
symbols.def: The admissible fixed endpoint-rule grammar in \(\mathrm{def:rule-language}\).

symbols.name: Hdl_SI
symbols.def: \(\mathsf{Hdl}_{\mathrm{SI}}\) is the observable synchronized Zhang--Dai rule-development handle in \(\mathrm{def:calculus-handle}\).

symbols.name: R_SI
symbols.def: \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{SI}}\) is the finite rule list derived by \(\mathrm{oeq:selection-lifting}\).

symbols.name: Cl_R
symbols.def: Least monotone closure of reported observed endpoints under \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{SI}}\), with the observational signature on \(U_0\) and every pooled-law signature on \(U_k\), \(k\in[K]\), used as fixed premises.

assumptions.condition: \(G_0(\eta)\) is a finite directed acyclic graph on the disjoint union \(V\cup S\).
No latent variable is a common cause of two vertices in \(V\).
Every node in \(S\) is childless in \(G_0(\eta)\).
For every \(j\in\{0,\ldots,K\}\), the regime-\(j\) joint law factorizes as \(\prod_{v\in V\cup S}\kappa_v^{(j)}(\eta)(dx_v\mid x_{\operatorname{pa}_{G_0(\eta)}(v)})\).
The event determined by \(S\) is generated in the basal world before every regime indexed by \(T(\eta)\).

For every comparison \(k\in[K]\), the pooled selected law \(P_{\eta,k}^{\mathrm{pool}}(dx,dz)=\tfrac12P_{\eta}^{(0)}(dx)\delta_0(dz)+\tfrac12P_{\eta}^{(k)}(dx)\delta_1(dz)\) on \(X\cup\{\zeta_k\}\) is faithful to \(M_k(\eta)\): for every disjoint vertex sets \(R_1,R_2,W\subseteq U_k\), \(X_{R_1}\mathbin{\perp\!\!\!\perp}X_{R_2}\mid X_W\) under \(P_{\eta,k}^{\mathrm{pool}}\) if and only if \(R_1\) and \(R_2\) are \(m\)-separated by \(W\) in \(M_k(\eta)\), with \(X_{\zeta_k}:=\zeta_k\).

definitions.name: Full oracle regime-MAG signature
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal O(\eta)=\bigl(\operatorname{skel}(M_k(\eta)),\operatorname{UC}(M_k(\eta))\bigr)_{k=0}^{K}\), with both operators evaluated on all of \(U_k\). The \(k=0\) conditional-independence input is the observational selected law \(P_{\eta}^{(0)}=\mathcal L_{\eta}(X\mid S^*=\mathbf 1)\) on \(U_0=V\), with no \(k\)-indexed indicator. For each \(k\in[K]\), the input is the pooled selected law \(P_{\eta,k}^{\mathrm{pool}}\) on \(X\cup\{\zeta_k\}\), whose arms are \(P_{\eta}^{(0)}\) and \(P_{\eta}^{(k)}\). Thus the signature includes every adjacency \(\zeta_k-v\) and every unshielded collider whose triple contains \(\zeta_k\), as well as every adjacency and unshielded collider entirely within \(V\).

definitions.name: Common-basal compatibility fiber
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal C(\mathcal O)=\{\eta\in\mathfrak M_{D,K}^{\mathrm{Dai}}:\bigl(\operatorname{skel}(M_k(\eta)),\operatorname{UC}(M_k(\eta))\bigr)_{k=0}^{K}=\mathcal O\}\). Each member supplies the observational selected law \(P_{\eta}^{(0)}=\mathcal L_{\eta}(X\mid S^*=\mathbf 1)\) for \(M_0(\eta)\) and, for every \(k\in[K]\), the pooled selected law \(P_{\eta,k}^{\mathrm{pool}}\) faithful to \(M_k(\eta)\); neither arm law is substituted for this pooled law. Equality preserves every adjacency and every unshielded collider on each full domain \(U_k\), including all indicator-involving instances.

definitions.name: Canonical endpoint-invariance SI-PAG
definitions.construction: For each reported observed endpoint \(e\in\mathcal E(\mathcal O)\), set \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{SI}}(\mathcal O)(e)=m\) if \(\mu_\eta(e)=m\in\{\mathtt{tail},\mathtt{arrow}\}\) for every \(\eta\in\mathcal C(\mathcal O)\), and set \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{SI}}(\mathcal O)(e)=\mathtt{circle}\) otherwise. The fiber \(\mathcal C(\mathcal O)\) is constrained by the observational signature associated with \(P_{\eta}^{(0)}\) on \(U_0=V\) and, for each \(k\in[K]\), by the full regime-MAG signature induced by \(P_{\eta,k}^{\mathrm{pool}}\) on \(U_k\), including indicator adjacencies and indicator-involving unshielded colliders, even though endpoints at \(\zeta_k\) are not part of the reported graph.

definitions.name: Fixed ancestral-selection compatibility fiber
definitions.construction: For \(\eta\in\mathcal C(\mathcal O)\), define \(\mathcal C_A(\mathcal O,\eta)=\{\widetilde\eta\in\mathcal C(\mathcal O):A(\widetilde\eta)=A(\eta)\}\).

definitions.name: Full observational Markov-equivalence input
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal O_0(\eta)=\mathcal I(M_0(\eta))\) is the conditional-independence signature associated with the observational selected law \(P_{\eta}^{(0)}=\mathcal L_{\eta}(X\mid S^*=\mathbf 1)\), where \(\mathcal I(M)\) is the complete set of conditional-independence relations entailed by \(m\)-separation in \(M\). At \(K=0\), this definition contains no regime index and no \(\zeta_k\).

definitions.name: Dai observational image fiber
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{Dai}}(\mathcal O_0)=\{M_0(\eta):\eta\in\mathfrak M_{D,0}^{\mathrm{Dai}},\ \mathcal O_0(\eta)=\mathcal O_0\}\) uses only \(P_{\eta}^{(0)}=\mathcal L_{\eta}(X\mid S^*=\mathbf 1)\); no intervention indicator is present.

definitions.name: Zhang observational PAG
definitions.construction: For each \(e\in\mathcal E_0(\mathcal O_0)\), set \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm Z}(\mathcal O_0)(e)=m\) if \(\nu_M(e)=m\in\{\mathtt{tail},\mathtt{arrow}\}\) for every \(M\in\mathcal C_{\mathrm{MAG}}(\mathcal O_0)\), and set \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm Z}(\mathcal O_0)(e)=\mathtt{circle}\) otherwise.

definitions.name: Signature-monotone selected graph
definitions.construction: For each \(\eta\in\mathcal C(\mathcal O)\), \(L_{A(\eta)}=(A(\eta),\{x\to y:xy\in H[A(\eta)],\ \sigma(x)\subseteq\sigma(y)\})\), with \(\operatorname{Reach}_{A(\eta)}(x,y)\) the nonempty directed reachability relation in \(L_{A(\eta)}\).

definitions.name: Observable selectedness-certificate closure
definitions.construction: Let \(C^{(0)}(\mathcal O)\subseteq V\) contain both observed endpoints of every observed--observed adjacency that is absent from the observational skeleton \(H\) and present in at least one intervention-regime skeleton in \(\mathcal O\). Recursively, let \(C^{(r+1)}(\mathcal O)\) equal \(C^{(r)}(\mathcal O)\) together with every middle vertex \(x\) of an observational unshielded noncollider \(i-x-j\) whose nonadjacent endpoints \(i,j\) lie in \(C^{(r)}(\mathcal O)\). Define \(\mathsf C_{\mathrm{sel}}(\mathcal O)=\bigcup_{r=0}^{|V|}C^{(r)}(\mathcal O)\), \(L_{\mathrm{cert}}(\mathcal O)=(\mathsf C_{\mathrm{sel}}(\mathcal O),\{x\to y:xy\in H[\mathsf C_{\mathrm{sel}}(\mathcal O)],\ \sigma(x)\subseteq\sigma(y)\})\), and let \(\operatorname{Reach}_{\mathrm{cert},\mathcal O}\) be nonempty directed reachability in this graph. Every ingredient is computed from \(\mathcal O\); no compatible model or latent set \(A(\eta)\) is queried.

definitions.name: Selected-subgraph replacement
definitions.construction: Given \(\eta\in\mathcal C(\mathcal O)\), define \(\operatorname{RepGraph}(\eta,B)=(\widetilde G_0,(\widetilde T_k)_{k=1}^{K})\) as follows. Replace the basal edge set by \(\bigl(E(G_0(\eta))\setminus E(G_0(\eta)[A(\eta)])\bigr)\cup E(B)\), add a childless pair-parent selection node for every edge of \(H[A(\eta)]\), and add a singleton-parent selection node for every vertex of \(A(\eta)\). For each \(k\in[K]\), retain \(T_k(\eta)\setminus A(\eta)\) and let \(\widetilde T_k\cap A(\eta)\) be the ancestry-minimal generators of \(Z_k\cap A(\eta)\) in \(\widetilde G_0\): \(v\in Z_k\cap A(\eta)\) is included exactly when it is not a proper descendant of another vertex of \(Z_k\cap A(\eta)\) or of a retained exterior direct target. This construction specifies only \(\widetilde G_0\) and \(\widetilde T_k\); it assigns no kernels and does not designate a replacement model.

definitions.name: Fully specified replacement realization fiber
definitions.construction: \(\operatorname{Real}(\eta,B)=\{\widetilde\eta\in\mathfrak M_{D,K}^{\mathrm{Dai}}:(G_0(\widetilde\eta),(T_k(\widetilde\eta))_{k=1}^{K})=\operatorname{RepGraph}(\eta,B)\}\). The defining predicate fixes the graphical and target components only; the kernel family \(\kappa(\widetilde\eta)\) is part of each fully specified member and is not inherited from \(\eta\).

definitions.name: Retained-edge sanity specification
definitions.construction: Set \(D=3\), \(K=1\), \(V=\{1,2,3\}\), and \(S=\{s\}\). Define \(\mathsf G_{\mathrm{san}}\) by the basal selected DAG \(E(G_0)=\{1\to2,2\to s\}\), with vertex \(3\) isolated in the basal DAG, and the direct soft-intervention target \(T_1=\{3\}\). No other basal edge or direct target is present.

definitions.name: Fixed SI endpoint-rule grammar
definitions.construction: \(\Lambda_{\mathrm{SI}}\) is the grammar of monotone endpoint rules with finitely many typed vertex and regime placeholders. Premises may use any adjacency or unshielded-collider predicate in the complete \(U_k\)-level signature \(\mathcal O\), where every \(k\in[K]\) input is the signature of the pooled selected law \(P_{\eta,k}^{\mathrm{pool}}\), including predicates whose vertices contain \(\zeta_k\), together with current observed-endpoint, uncovered-path, discriminating-path, membership in the observable certificate set \(\mathsf C_{\mathrm{sel}}(\mathcal O)\), and reachability in \(L_{\mathrm{cert}}(\mathcal O)\); conclusions replace reported observed circles by tails or arrowheads. No rule premise may mention \(A(\eta)\), \(L_{A(\eta)}\), a member of \(\mathcal C(\mathcal O)\), a realizability oracle, or a model enumerator.

definitions.name: Observable synchronized Zhang--Dai construction handle
definitions.construction: \(\mathsf{Hdl}_{\mathrm{SI}}\): start from Zhang's rules R0--R10 on the observational signature on \(U_0=V\), which is associated with \(P_{\eta}^{(0)}=\mathcal L_{\eta}(X\mid S^*=\mathbf 1)\), and on each \(k\in[K]\) full signature on \(U_k\), which is associated with the pooled selected law \(P_{\eta,k}^{\mathrm{pool}}\). Compute \(\mathsf C_{\mathrm{sel}}(\mathcal O)\) from intervention-created adjacencies and observational-unshielded-noncollider closure, then propagate forbidden signature transitions only along shortest uncovered paths certified by \(\operatorname{Reach}_{\mathrm{cert},\mathcal O}\). Enforce Dai et al.'s Lemma 5 disjunction \(Z_k=T_k(\eta)\cup((F_k(\eta)\setminus T_k(\eta))\cap A(\eta))\) only as a witness obligation, without identifying \(T_k(\eta)\) with \(Z_k\). Use \(L_{A(\eta)}\), \(\operatorname{RepGraph}(\eta,B)\), and \(\operatorname{Real}(\eta,B)\) only in the completeness proof to extend or oppose marks after an observable rule fires; none is a rule premise. The handle derives the finite list in \(\Lambda_{\mathrm{SI}}\) from observable predicates alone.

definitions.name: Rule closure
definitions.construction: \(\operatorname{Cl}_{\mathcal R}(\mathcal O)\) is initialized with every skeleton and every unshielded collider in the complete regime-MAG signatures on \(U_k\). The observational component is associated with \(P_{\eta}^{(0)}=\mathcal L_{\eta}(X\mid S^*=\mathbf 1)\); each non-observational signature is supplied by \(P_{\eta,k}^{\mathrm{pool}}\) and includes all \(\zeta_k\)-involving instances. It treats this full input signature as immutable premises and repeatedly applies every instance of every rule in \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{SI}}\) until no reported observed circle endpoint changes.

statements.statement: Fix \(\eta\in\mathcal C(\mathcal O)\). If \(B\) is acyclic, every edge of \(B\) lies in \(H[A(\eta)]\), \(B\) creates no unshielded collider whose endpoints are nonadjacent in \(H\), and every \(x\to y\in B\) satisfies \(\sigma(x)\subseteq\sigma(y)\), then the basal DAG \(\widetilde G_0\) in \(\operatorname{RepGraph}(\eta,B)\) satisfies \(\operatorname{An}_{\widetilde G_0}(\operatorname{pa}_{\widetilde G_0}(S))\cap V=A(\eta)\). For every \(k=0,\ldots,K\), the twin graph determined by \(\operatorname{RepGraph}(\eta,B)\) has a latent-projection MAG on \(U_k\) with exactly the adjacency and unshielded-collider signature of \(M_k(\eta)\), including every adjacency and every unshielded collider involving \(\zeta_k\). For \(k\in[K]\), its target and descendant data realize \(Z_k=\widetilde T_k\cup((\operatorname{de}_{\widetilde G_0}(\widetilde T_k)\cap V\setminus\widetilde T_k)\cap A(\eta))\), with the two terms representing direct targets and indirectly affected ancestrally selected vertices separately.
statements.justification: This lemma isolates the graph-theoretic obligation: the replacement specification preserves the full oracle signature before any probability law is chosen.
statements.gap: Dai et al., Lemmas 4--6 on pp. 6--7, give the intervention-created adjacency, indicator-neighbor, and endpoint semantics used here, but do not give a synchronized common-basal graph replacement preserving every indicator-involving signature constraint.
statements.consumer: It supplies the graphical half of each opposing selected-endpoint witness used by the complete calculus.

statements.statement: Under the hypotheses of \(\mathrm{lem:graphical\mbox{-}replacement\mbox{-}preservation}\), there exist finite-alphabet local kernels \(\widetilde\kappa=(\widetilde\kappa_v^{(j)})_{v\in V\cup S,\ 0\le j\le K}\) factoring over the basal DAG in \(\operatorname{RepGraph}(\eta,B)\), satisfying \(\widetilde\kappa_v^{(k)}=\widetilde\kappa_v^{(0)}\) for every \(v\notin\widetilde T_k\), and assigning positive probability to \(S^*=\mathbf 1\), such that the resulting fully specified model \(\widetilde\eta\) belongs to \(\operatorname{Real}(\eta,B)\). Simultaneously for every \(k\in[K]\), the selected pooled law \(P_{\widetilde\eta,k}^{\mathrm{pool}}\) is faithful to \(M_k(\widetilde\eta)\). The kernels \(\widetilde\kappa\) are constructed jointly across regimes and need not equal \(\kappa(\eta)\).
statements.justification: A genuine joint kernel construction, rather than graph preservation alone, is required to prove that the replacement specification has a faithful Dai-class realization.
statements.gap: Generic single-DAG faithfulness does not by itself produce one family of selected arm laws whose pooled indicator laws are simultaneously faithful to all replacement regime MAGs.
statements.consumer: It turns each graphical endpoint modification into a statistically well-defined whole-family witness.

statements.statement: For every \(\eta\in\mathcal C(\mathcal O)\) and every \(B\) satisfying the admissibility conditions in \(\mathrm{lem:graphical\mbox{-}replacement\mbox{-}preservation}\), there exists \(\widetilde\eta\in\operatorname{Real}(\eta,B)\) such that \(A(\widetilde\eta)=A(\eta)\) and \(\mathcal O(\widetilde\eta)=\mathcal O(\eta)=\mathcal O\). Hence \(\widetilde\eta\) has the well-defined observational selected law \(P_{\widetilde\eta}^{(0)}=\mathcal L_{\widetilde\eta}(X\mid S^*=\mathbf 1)\) and, for every \(k\in[K]\), a faithful pooled law \(P_{\widetilde\eta,k}^{\mathrm{pool}}\); it preserves every adjacency and every unshielded collider on every full domain \(U_k\), including all \(\zeta_k\)-involving instances, and for every \(k\in[K]\) satisfies \(Z_k=T_k(\widetilde\eta)\cup((F_k(\widetilde\eta)\setminus T_k(\widetilde\eta))\cap A(\widetilde\eta))\). No equality between \(\kappa(\widetilde\eta)\) and \(\kappa(\eta)\) is required.
statements.justification: This synthesis theorem supplies a fully specified replacement model with the same complete oracle signature and ancestral selected set.
statements.gap: Published equivalence results do not prove existence of faithful selected-law realizations for a synchronized replacement specification.
statements.consumer: It supplies valid whole-family witnesses for selected-selected circles in the sciPlex2 graph.

statements.statement: There exists a finite-alphabet model \(\eta^\dagger\in\mathfrak M_{3,1}^{\mathrm{Dai}}\) whose graph and target data equal \(\mathsf G_{\mathrm{san}}\). For every such faithful model, \(A(\eta^\dagger)=\{1,2\}\), \(Z_1=\{3\}\), and Dai et al.'s retained-edge result gives \(1\to2\) in \(M_1(\eta^\dagger)\). Consequently, the endpoint at vertex \(2\) on that retained adjacency is an arrowhead although \(2\notin Z_1\). The corrected endpoint frontier therefore makes its arrowhead equivalence only for intervention-created adjacencies \(uv\notin H\); it makes no target-membership equivalence for retained adjacencies \(uv\in H\).
statements.justification: The explicit three-variable reduction separates retained basal orientation from the target-driven orientation mechanism and removes the failed normalization.
statements.gap: Dai et al., Lemma 6 on p. 7, supplies retained-edge semantics; target membership controls intervention-created adjacencies through a distinct mechanism and cannot characterize retained-edge arrowheads.
statements.consumer: It gives an executable unit check for any implementation of the fixed-selected-set endpoint frontier.

statements.statement: For every \(\eta\in\mathcal C(\mathcal O)\), where the interventional components of \(\mathcal O\) are induced by the faithful pooled selected laws \(P_{\eta,k}^{\mathrm{pool}}\), fix \(k\in[K]\) and an intervention-created observed adjacency \(uv\) with \(u,v\in A(\eta)\), meaning that \(uv\) is absent from the observational skeleton \(H\) and present in the regime-\(k\) skeleton. Over \(\mathcal C_A(\mathcal O,\eta)\), an arrowhead at \(u\) on \(uv\) is feasible if and only if \(u\in Z_k\), and a tail at \(u\) is feasible if and only if \(u\notin Z_k\) or \(\operatorname{Reach}_{A(\eta)}(u,v)=1\). Here \(u\in Z_k\) means that \(u\) is either a direct target or an indirectly affected ancestrally selected variable, not that \(u\in T_k(\eta)\). Every feasible mark is attained by a whole-family common-basal model in \(\mathcal C_A(\mathcal O,\eta)\) preserving the full pooled-law signatures on \(U_k\). Retained adjacencies \(uv\in H\) are outside this target-membership equivalence and retain any arrowheads supplied by basal directed structure, as in \(\mathrm{prop:retained\mbox{-}edge\mbox{-}sanity\mbox{-}reduction}\).
statements.justification: The theorem gives the exact target-and-reachability frontier for the intervention-created selected adjacencies to which that mechanism applies.
statements.gap: Dai et al., Lemmas 4--6 on pp. 6--7, give fixed-model adjacency, indicator-neighbor, and endpoint semantics; they do not prove the reverse common-basal witness construction over a fixed-\(A(\eta)\) equivalence fiber.
statements.consumer: The result classifies which intervention-created selected-gene endpoints can remain biological ambiguity after selection membership is certified.

statements.statement: For every \(\eta\in\mathfrak M_{D,K}^{\mathrm{Dai}}\), with \(\mathcal O=\mathcal O(\eta)\) formed from the faithful pooled selected laws \(P_{\eta,k}^{\mathrm{pool}}\), if \(uv\) is absent from the observational skeleton \(H\) and present in an observed intervention-regime skeleton, then \(u,v\in A(\eta)\).
statements.justification: Dai et al.'s Lemma 4 supplies the initial visible-selectedness certificate used by the rule handle.
statements.gap: Dai et al., Lemma 4 on p. 6, is the published source of this intervention-created-adjacency certificate; the closure of partially certified selection membership is not part of that lemma.
statements.consumer: It initializes cross-regime selectedness without analyst-supplied labels.

statements.statement: For every \(\eta\in\mathfrak M_{D,K}^{\mathrm{Dai}}\), with \(\mathcal O=\mathcal O(\eta)\) formed from the faithful pooled selected laws \(P_{\eta,k}^{\mathrm{pool}}\), the entirely observable closure satisfies \(\mathsf C_{\mathrm{sel}}(\mathcal O)\subseteq A(\eta)\). The seed inclusion is Dai et al.'s intervention-created-adjacency certificate. At each recursive step, if \(i,j\in\mathsf C_{\mathrm{sel}}(\mathcal O)\) are the nonadjacent endpoints of an observational unshielded noncollider \(i-x-j\), then \(x\in A(\eta)\), so adjoining \(x\) preserves the inclusion.
statements.justification: This theorem turns the noncollider closure into an observable sound certificate set that can legally appear in rule premises.
statements.gap: Dai et al., Lemma 4 on p. 6, provides the cross-regime seed but does not state this noncollider closure; Wang, Du, and Zhou instead take singleton background knowledge as supplied.
statements.consumer: It supplies the model-free selectedness predicate used by the local calculus while reserving \(A(\eta)\) for completeness witnesses.

statements.statement: Using \(\mathsf{Hdl}_{\mathrm{SI}}\), derive a finite rule list \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{SI}}\subset\Lambda_{\mathrm{SI}}\), independent of \(D\) and \(K\), whose premises use only the full signature \(\mathcal O\), current endpoint marks, \(\mathsf C_{\mathrm{sel}}(\mathcal O)\), and \(\operatorname{Reach}_{\mathrm{cert},\mathcal O}\), and determine whether its saturation has the following extension property. For every compatible full signature \(\mathcal O\), whose observational component is associated with \(P_{\eta}^{(0)}=\mathcal L_{\eta}(X\mid S^*=\mathbf 1)\) and whose \(k\in[K]\) components are obtained from faithful pooled selected laws on \(X\cup\{\zeta_k\}\), and every residual reported circle endpoint \(e\in\mathcal E(\mathcal O)\), there are \(\eta_{\mathtt{tail}},\eta_{\mathtt{arrow}}\in\mathcal C(\mathcal O)\) with opposite marks at \(e\), each a fully specified model generated by one basal selected DAG on \(V\cup S\) and one jointly constructed kernel family satisfying non-target kernel stability across all regimes, while agreeing with every observed mark fixed by saturation and preserving every adjacency and every unshielded collider on each \(U_k\), including all \(\zeta_k\)-involving instances. Each witness supplies \(P_{\eta_\star}^{(0)}=\mathcal L_{\eta_\star}(X\mid S^*=\mathbf 1)\) for the observational component and, for each \(k\in[K]\), \(P_{\eta_\star,k}^{\mathrm{pool}}\), not a single-arm surrogate, as the faithful law of the preserved intervention-regime MAG. For each witness \(\eta_\star\) and each regime \(k\in[K]\), it must realize \(Z_k=T_k(\eta_\star)\cup((F_k(\eta_\star)\setminus T_k(\eta_\star))\cap A(\eta_\star))\), handling direct targets and indirectly affected ancestrally selected variables separately rather than setting \(T_k(\eta_\star)=Z_k\). The proof may use \(A(\eta_\star)\) and \(L_{A(\eta_\star)}\) after a witness has been chosen, but the rule system may neither guess these latent objects nor invoke a global realizability query.
statements.justification: This is the genuine unresolved step between conditional selected-set witnesses and a complete observable local calculus.
statements.gap: Dai et al., Theorem 3 and the discussion on p. 8, lines 646--662, prove CDIS soundness and explicitly leave completeness uncertain because no complete rules are known for their Lemma 6 background knowledge. Zhang, Sections 3--4 and Theorem 2, proves arrowhead and tail completeness for one observational PAG by constructing representative MAGs, but does not synchronize intervention regimes. The Zhou--Kocaoglu author listing at lines 27--31 and the public abstract record at lines 5--9 verify a known-target enumeration-based completion; official theorem numbering and text were inaccessible, so no formula-level comparison is made. None of these sources supplies the unknown-selection common-exterior lift posed here.
statements.consumer: A positive answer certifies every circle in Dai et al.'s A549 analysis; a negative answer gives a concrete obstruction requiring a richer equivalence-class representation.

statements.statement: There exists a single finite \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{SI}}\subset\Lambda_{\mathrm{SI}}\), with rule schemata independent of \(D\) and \(K\), such that for every \(\eta\in\mathfrak M_{D,K}^{\mathrm{Dai}}\), \(\operatorname{Cl}_{\mathcal R}(\mathcal O(\eta))=\mathcal P_{\mathrm{SI}}(\mathcal O(\eta))\) on \(\mathcal E(\mathcal O(\eta))\). The input \(\mathcal O(\eta)\) is the full collection of regime-MAG adjacencies and unshielded colliders on \(U_k\): the observational component on \(U_0=V\) is associated with \(P_{\eta}^{(0)}=\mathcal L_{\eta}(X\mid S^*=\mathbf 1)\), and every \(k\in[K]\) regime MAG is the faithful graphical law of \(P_{\eta,k}^{\mathrm{pool}}\) on \(X\cup\{\zeta_k\}\), including all \(\zeta_k\)-involving instances, while the equality reports observed endpoints. Equivalently, the rules are sound and every reported endpoint left circular has both a tail and an arrowhead whole-family realization in \(\mathcal C(\mathcal O(\eta))\), with each realization a fully specified model sharing one basal selected DAG on \(V\cup S\) across its regimes, carrying its own kernel family with unchanged non-target kernels, supplying its own observational selected law and faithful pooled selected laws, and preserving the entire full-regime signature.
statements.justification: Equality with the canonical endpoint invariant is the theorem-level structure-identification kernel.
statements.gap: Dai et al., Theorem 3 and p. 8, lines 646--662, prove CDIS soundness and explicitly leave completeness open. Zhang, Sections 3--4 and Theorem 2, establishes single-PAG arrowhead and tail completeness, not common-basal synchronization. The Zhou--Kocaoglu author listing at lines 27--31 and public abstract at lines 5--9 describe known-target completion by compatible-MAG enumeration; official theorem numbering and text were inaccessible, so only the abstract-level distinction is used.
statements.consumer: The theorem makes a retained A549 circle an identified equivalence-class feature rather than evidence of an unfinished orientation algorithm.

statements.statement: Fix \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{SI}}\subset\Lambda_{\mathrm{SI}}\). If every rule premise and path predicate is decidable uniformly in time polynomial in \(D\), \(K\), and the encoding length of \(\mathcal O\), and every conclusion changes a reported circle endpoint once to a tail or arrowhead, then saturation makes at most \(2(K+1)D(D-1)\) strict reported-endpoint updates and computes \(\operatorname{Cl}_{\mathcal R}(\mathcal O)\) in polynomial time. The observational skeleton and unshielded colliders on \(U_0=V\), together with the complete skeletons and unshielded-collider families of the faithful pooled selected-law signatures on \(U_k\), \(k\in[K]\), including all indicator adjacencies and indicator-involving unshielded colliders, remain immutable inputs. If additionally \(\operatorname{Cl}_{\mathcal R}(\mathcal O)=\mathcal P_{\mathrm{SI}}(\mathcal O)\), this polynomial output is the canonical SI-PAG and no enumeration of \(\mathcal C(\mathcal O)\) is required.
statements.justification: This conditional closure-accounting corollary records the computational consequence of a fixed finite grammar and one-way endpoint updates.
statements.gap: The proposition is not an independent novelty claim; its substantive identification content comes entirely from the complete-calculus theorem.
statements.consumer: An implementation can audit rule-predicate complexity before using complete saturation on a perturbation panel.

sampling_model.design: Deterministic oracle identification from the observational MAG signature and \(K\) intervention-regime MAG signatures generated by one common basal selected DAG.
sampling_model.units: The primitive object is a fully specified member \(\eta\in\mathfrak M_{D,K}^{\mathrm{Dai}}\). At \(K=0\), its only oracle law is \(P_{\eta}^{(0)}=\mathcal L_{\eta}(X\mid S^*=\mathbf 1)\); at \(K\ge 1\), each comparison additionally uses \(P_{\eta,k}^{\mathrm{pool}}\) on \(X\cup\{\zeta_k\}\).
sampling_model.treatment: Regime membership is observed, while every direct soft-intervention target set \(T_k(\eta)\) is latent and may differ from the indicator-neighbor set \(Z_k\).
sampling_model.overlap: The common pre-treatment selection event has positive probability, so every selected oracle law is well defined.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Not applicable; the proposal begins from exact regime-MAG adjacency and unshielded-collider inputs.

estimand_functional: \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{SI}}(\mathcal O)(e)=m\iff\mu_\eta(e)=m\text{ for every }\eta\in\mathcal C(\mathcal O);\quad \mathcal P_{\mathrm{SI}}(\mathcal O)(e)=\mathtt{circle}\text{ otherwise}\)

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 3 proves CDIS soundness, while p. 8, lines 652--661, says completeness remains uncertain and is conjectured.
Sections 3--4 establish arrowhead and tail completeness for the observational PAG rules, with Theorem 2 providing the representative-MAG construction.
Two maximal ancestral graphs are Markov equivalent if and only if they have the same adjacencies and colliders with order.
The public abstract, lines 5--9, describes a known-target enumeration-based completion that is sound and theoretically complete; official theorem text was inaccessible.
We present the first polynomial-delay MAG listing method.
We provide a complete characterization of the equivalence class under soft interventions with unknown targets.
We develop a provably sound and complete algorithm, F-FCI, using both observational and interventional data.

tldr: Selection before perturbation couples every regime-specific MAG through one common basal selected DAG, so completing the regimes independently can miss endpoints compelled by their joint origin. The deterministic kernel is a fixed finite within-regime and cross-regime rule calculus whose monotone closure equals the canonical observed-endpoint SI-PAG for Dai et al.'s causally sufficient, unknown-target twin-graph class. A graph replacement lemma and a simultaneous faithful-kernel realization lemma yield an exact frontier for intervention-created selected--selected endpoints conditional on the ancestral selected set. The open mathematical step lifts these witnesses through unknown selection membership and a common exterior completion, producing opposing common-basal realizations for every endpoint left circular. If the fixed rules have uniformly polynomial matchers, monotone saturation uses only polynomially many strict endpoint updates.

project_justification.gap: Dai et al., Theorem 3 and p. 8, lines 646--662, prove CDIS soundness and explicitly leave completeness uncertain because complete rules for their Lemma 6 background knowledge are unavailable. Their Lemmas 4--6 on pp. 6--7 supply the fixed-model semantic inputs but not opposing common-basal representatives. Zhang, Sections 3--4 and Theorem 2, proves arrowhead and tail completeness for one observational PAG without joint regime realizability. The Zhou--Kocaoglu author listing at lines 27--31 and public abstract at lines 5--9 describe an enumeration-based completion in a known-target setting; official theorem numbering and text were inaccessible, so no formula-level claim is used.
project_justification.niche: The missing object is a dimension- and regime-count-independent endpoint calculus for unknown-target interventions after common pre-treatment selection, together with a semantic guarantee that every residual circle is genuine common-basal ambiguity.
project_justification.fill: The project combines full regime-MAG adjacency and unshielded-collider signatures with observable selectedness certificates, signature-monotone path propagation, graph replacement, and simultaneous faithful-kernel realization. It proves the fixed-\(A(\eta)\) endpoint frontier, solves the unknown-selection lifting problem, derives a complete fixed local calculus, and obtains conditional polynomial saturation without enumerating compatible basal DAGs.

related_work: Dai et al., Lemmas 4--6 on pp. 6--7, characterize intervention-created observed adjacencies, indicator neighbors, and endpoint semantics in the destination pre-treatment-selection twin class. Their Theorem 3 and the explicit discussion on p. 8, lines 646--662, prove CDIS soundness and leave completeness uncertain because complete orientation rules for the Lemma 6 background knowledge are not known. Zhang's primary article separates arrowhead and tail completeness in Sections 3--4; its Theorem 2 constructs a representative MAG and completes one observational PAG, but does not synchronize several intervention projections through one basal selected DAG. Ali, Richardson, and Spirtes characterize equivalence of a single MAG through adjacencies and ordered colliders; those invariants guide the replacement lemma but do not enforce a common basal fiber. The Zhou--Kocaoglu author publication listing, entry 2 at lines 27--31, verifies Zihan Zhou and Murat Kocaoglu, the title, ICML 2026, and the venue. Its public abstract record, paper 1 at lines 5--9, says that known-target interventional FCI can be incomplete, describes a complete compatible-MAG enumeration, and describes extra local rules only as a tightening. The official OpenReview theorem numbering and text were inaccessible, so this proposal makes no formula-level claim about that paper. Wang, Du, and Zhou give polynomial-delay MAG listing and locally complete propagation under singleton background knowledge; their work informs only the conditional saturation accounting, while selectedness here is derived from the multi-regime oracle signature. Jaber et al., p. 2 and Theorem 3 on p. 7, assume no selection bias and prove completeness for their unknown-target soft-intervention equivalence class, so they do not cover pre-treatment twin coupling. Luo et al.'s public ICLR 2026 record describes F-FCI for latent confounding with post-treatment selection; that timing and fine-grained interventional fiber are distinct from the causally sufficient common-basal pre-treatment-selected class here.
technical_internal_limitation: The fixed-\(A(\eta)\) replacement theorem does not solve the headline problem. \(\operatorname{RepGraph}(\eta,B)\) is a graphical specification, and preservation of skeletons and unshielded colliders alone does not make \(\operatorname{Real}(\eta,B)\) nonempty; that requires a joint faithful-kernel realization. Beyond fixed \(A(\eta)\), selection membership may vary over \(\mathcal C(\mathcal O)\), a single exterior DAG completion must serve every regime, and \(Z_k\) identifies a union of direct targets and indirectly affected ancestrally selected vertices. A proof that sets \(T_k(\eta)=Z_k\), guesses \(A(\eta)\), completes regimes independently, or invokes a global basal-DAG enumerator does not establish \(\mathrm{oeq:selection\mbox{-}lifting}\).
honest_scope: The graph replacement, simultaneous faithful-kernel realization, combined replacement theorem, and intervention-created-edge frontier conditional on \(A(\eta)\) are theorem candidates and remain to be proved for the complete regime signatures. The retained-edge sanity reduction records why basal adjacencies lie outside that frontier. The full finite rule list, unknown-selection-membership lift, common exterior completion, separation of direct targets from indirectly affected selected vertices, and residual-circle witnesses are open and central. The complete-calculus theorem is deliberately downstream of \(\mathrm{oeq:selection\mbox{-}lifting}\). At \(K=0\), the sole selected law is \(P_{\eta}^{(0)}=\mathcal L_{\eta}(X\mid S^*=\mathbf 1)\), with no \(k\) or \(\zeta_k\); the Dai observational image is contained in the unrestricted observational MAG fiber, so every Zhang-compelled endpoint remains compelled, but equality of the fibers is not claimed. For \(K\ge 1\), each intervention comparison uses its binary-indicator pooled law on \(X\cup\{\zeta_k\}\). The proposal excludes latent basal common causes, post-treatment selection, regime-specific selection mechanisms, and global basal-DAG enumeration as the headline method.

novelty_justification: The closest result is Dai et al. (ICLR 2025): Lemmas 4--6 on pp. 6--7 define the fixed-model semantics, while Theorem 3 and p. 8, lines 646--662, prove soundness and explicitly leave CDIS completeness unresolved. Zhang, Sections 3--4 and Theorem 2, is the closest fixed-calculus completeness result, but it concerns one observational PAG rather than a common-basal regime family. The Zhou--Kocaoglu author listing at lines 27--31 and public abstract at lines 5--9 describe a known-target procedure that obtains completeness by compatible-MAG enumeration; official theorem numbering and text were inaccessible, so no formula-level comparison is asserted. The strict gap is a fixed finite observable endpoint calculus for the unknown-target common-basal fiber, plus whole-family opposing witnesses for every residual circle. The fixed-\(A(\eta)\) signature-monotone frontier is the supporting theorem that separates this kernel from observational PAG completeness.
